_what_this_is: The complete, authoritative list of files permitted to carry the published test count. Committed data, not prose. It exists because 'nine surfaces' was once inherited from a label whose own components summed to ten, and nobody checked — the same trusting-prose-over-measurement error that produced a false claim about verify_seo gating CI.
_enforcement: tests/test_published_count_manifest.py enumerates tracked files and fails on a count literal outside current carriers and exact centrally classified dated records. Broad path exclusions are forbidden; discovery, provenance, rename and content-hash failures fail closed.
_canonical_source: data/site_facts.json -> counts.tests.total_collected, produced by scripts/site_facts.count_tests() from `pytest --collect-only`. The number is generated, never hand-authored.

non_surface_carriers.note: The canonical artefact itself. Regenerated by scripts/site_facts.py; never edited by hand.
Carries the canonical hint key used by --verify-facts to recognise the fact in prose. Tooling, not a published claim.

_historical_records: Exact dated-evidence classifications live in data/count_record_classes.json. Broad path exclusions are forbidden.
_added_2026_07_31: docs/architecture.md joined the list after it was found publishing '1,223 tests' against a canonical of 2,618 at the moment of discovery (short by 1,395 at that instant; the canonical rose during the session as tests were added), while absent from this manifest and from claim_auditor.VERIFY_FACTS_FILES. scripts/claim_auditor.py:1109-1114 had recorded that exact gap as known and parked. A hand-maintained list cannot prove its own completeness, so the backstop is now tests/test_cascade_count.py::TestEveryPublishedSurfaceCarriesTheCanonicalCount, which enumerates tracked .md/.html/.txt with git ls-files instead of reading this file (measurement rule 4c).
